findings.issue: ἁλῶνται represents the contracted present of the verb meaning “wander,” usually cited as ἀλάομαι. It does not support the draft’s capture sense or the note’s alternative “convicted.” The supplied rough breathing is not grounds for substituting a different verb or treating the verified print as corrupt.
findings.suggested_revision: Render “they wander here.” Replace the lexical note with an explanation of literal wandering versus contextual straying or wandering in error. Preserve the supplied Greek spelling; no print correction is required.

findings.source_quote: οὐ γὰρ βούλομαι στρέμματα γίνεσθαι εἰς ἡμᾶς τῶν πολιτῶν
findings.english_quote: I do not want the citizens to turn against us.
findings.issue: The hostile interpretation is a contextual choice, not an unambiguous equivalent. στρέμματα denotes turnings or contortions, and εἰς ἡμᾶς directs them toward the visitors. Turning toward them to look, without necessarily becoming hostile, is a material alternative supported by the warning against entering as a large group. The note mentions literal turnings but explains only adverse reactions, resentment, or disturbances.
findings.suggested_revision: Explicitly compare the source-transparent candidate “I do not want the citizens turning toward us” with the current hostile reading. Preserve the alternative of attracting the citizens’ attention or causing them to turn and look, and explain why the selected rendering favors either attention or antagonism. A revised text or note must receive fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Γένος μὲν καὶ πατρίδα εἰπεῖν οὐκ οἶμαι πεῖσαί ποτε δυνηθῆναί τινα
findings.english_quote: As for my lineage and homeland, I do not think anyone could ever persuade me to tell them.
findings.issue: The main rendering is defensible, but its note incorrectly presents the attachment of τινα as grammatically determined. τινα can instead be understood as the object of πεῖσαι, with the woman as the understood subject of δυνηθῆναι: she does not think she could convince anyone when stating her descent and homeland. That reading concerns the credibility of her account, rather than unwillingness to disclose it, and is contextually supported by the contrast between her present condition and her claimed noble birth.
findings.suggested_revision: If retaining the main text, revise the note to state that it takes τινα as the subject of δυνηθῆναι and supplies the woman as the object of πεῖσαι. Preserve the alternative: “As for stating my lineage and homeland, I do not think I could ever convince anyone.” Explain that the chosen reading favors reluctance to disclose in light of her following question, while the alternative favors anticipated disbelief. Do not describe either attachment as compulsory; the revised note requires fresh review.
